Eatwell Guide page: five food groups, shows proportions of each in a balanced diet.
Eatwell page: fruit/veg and starchy each just over a third; 8 tips page: choose higher-fibre starchy foods.
8 tips page: five a day and at least 2 portions of fish a week, 1 oily. Wording 'a variety' came from the author's note; the search text said 'aim for five a day'.
Eatwell page: foods high in fat, salt or sugar sit outside the guide and should be eaten less often and in smaller amounts.

Eatwell page: guide shows how much of each food group should make up a healthy balanced diet.
Eatwell page: foods high in fat, salt or sugar sit outside the guide; less often, smaller amounts.
Eatwell page: fruit and vegetables just over a third of what we eat.
8 tips page: aim for five a day. 'Variety' not shown in returned text but is standard NHS wording.
8 tips page: a portion of fresh, canned or frozen fruit and veg is 80g.
Eatwell page: starchy foods just over a third; 8 tips: higher-fibre/wholegrain (wholewheat pasta, brown rice, potatoes with skins).

Eatwell/balanced diet pages: choose lower-fat and lower-sugar dairy or alternatives.
Balanced diet page: choose unsaturated oils and spreads and eat them in small amounts.
The 8 tips page covers cutting down on saturated fat and sugar and eating less salt, but 'the main things to keep in check' is the author's framing.

claims.evidence: Water, drinks page: combined total of fruit juice, vegetable juice and smoothies should not exceed 150ml a day; unsweetened versions are still high in free sugar.
Water, drinks page: swap sugary drinks for diet, sugar-free or no-added-sugar drinks.
The 8 tips page says a healthy balanced diet helps maintain a healthy weight and exercise may reduce risk of serious conditions; 'energy in and out is the key' was not found in returned text.
claims.newSentence: The NHS tips say that a healthy, balanced diet can help maintain a healthy weight, and that regular exercise may help reduce the risk of serious health conditions.

claims.evidence: 8 tips page: a healthy breakfast high in fibre and low in fat, sugar and salt can form part of a balanced diet.
Salt: the facts page: no more than 6g a day for adults and children aged 11 and over; younger children have lower limits.
Salt: the facts page: about three quarters of the salt we eat comes from packaged and everyday foods. 'Which is why labels matter' is the author's inference.
claims.newSentence: The NHS says around three quarters of the salt people eat comes from packaged and everyday foods.

claims.evidence: Salt: the facts page: high salt can raise blood pressure, which increases risk of heart disease and stroke.
Facts about fat page: too much saturated fat raises LDL cholesterol and heart disease risk; unsaturated fats from vegetable oils, oily fish, avocados; replace saturated with unsaturated.
Food labels returned text: back-of-pack table lists energy, fat, saturates, carbohydrate, sugars, protein and salt.
Traffic light labels colour-code fat, saturates, sugars and salt: green low, amber medium, red high (NHS Trust/GOV.UK Check the label pages; same scheme).

Sugar: the facts page lists sweets, sugary drinks, cakes, biscuits, pastries, breakfast cereals as sources; alcoholic drinks were not found in the returned text. Label/ingredients checking is supported.
claims.newSentence: The NHS lists sweets, sugary drinks, cakes, biscuits, pastries and breakfast cereals among common sources of added sugar, and says the label and ingredients list can show how much sugar a food contains.

notes: Searches blend pages; numbers (80g, 150ml, 6g, 5 portions) were each seen in returned NHS text. Traffic-light and label entries rest on NHS Trust / GOV.UK text of the same scheme. Searches capped at 10.
